summary: P0 SSOT Persistence — FRONTEND validation. Verified via live Playwright run against production preview URL that (a) a full workspace investigation saved to /api/cases/save with the SSOT bundle can be restored from the Case Library drawer with ZERO recomputation (no /api/die/understand, /api/die/analyze or /api/die/narrate calls fired) and (b) a legacy case (saved without ssot) triggers the fallback path that DOES re-fire all three /die/* endpoints. Status ribbons match the spec exactly. All P0 acceptance criteria PASS.

issues: Informational (task called out as non-blocker): case rows do NOT visually differentiate SSOT-backed vs legacy cases. The GET /api/cases response includes has_ssot per case, but the drawer does not render any badge/pill (e.g. '📦 SSOT v1.0' vs '⚠ legacy'). Would help analysts predict restore behaviour before clicking OPEN.

action_items: OPTIONAL (informational, not a P0 blocker): add a visual badge in CasesDrawer.jsx to differentiate has_ssot=true vs has_ssot=false rows so analysts can tell at-a-glance which cases will restore instantly vs recompute.
critical_code_review_comments: WorkspacePage.jsx line 2418: <VerdictCard/> render is commented out (`{/* {verdictCard && (<VerdictCard verdict={verdictCard} testidPrefix="workspace-verdict" />)} */}`). The saveCase() bundle still ships verdict_card in the SSOT and rehydrateFromHistory / CasesDrawer onRestore both restore it into state — but nothing in the workspace actually paints it any more. Either delete the dead state/prop plumbing or re-enable the render. Not a P0 SSOT blocker (Analyst Brief and Investigation panels render fine from SSOT), but tests using [data-testid=verdict-card] will always miss.

WorkspacePage.jsx is 3631 lines — well above the 700-line guideline. Splitting SaveCase / CasesDrawer restore / rehydrateFromHistory into a `useCaseHydration` hook would reduce cognitive load and make the SSOT contract single-sourced (currently duplicated at ~L393 rehydrateFromHistory and ~L3451 CasesDrawer onRestore).

The legacy fallback (WorkspacePage.jsx L3527-3546) fires three uncoordinated api.post() calls with no cancellation on unmount and no combined loading indicator — if the analyst closes the case mid-recompute the promises still resolve into stale setState. Consider AbortController + a single legacy_recompute() helper.

success_rate.frontend: 100% on P0 SSOT acceptance criteria (5/5 core assertions passed; 1 non-P0 selector miss on commented-out VerdictCard)
